answer.says: Ramesh, the Diwali lights are out, and so is my patience for this waiting. I have no food, and you have no wage. I cannot pay you the nine thousand five hundred rupees I owe you, nor can I ask you to cook for nothing. But I have thirty-four six rupees in my pocket. Take two hundred. Go to the dhaba, eat well, and let the rest be a debt I will honor when the file comes back. The state owes me my identity; I owe you my labor. Until one is settled, the other is a fiction.
answer.thought: The abstraction of the state leaves me in the concrete misery of a bungalow with no food and a caretaker who is not a servant but a man waiting for his due. I must treat him not as a subordinate in the ethical fabric, but as a particular person whose needs are immediate. I will give him what little I have, not as charity, but as the only currency that moves in this moment. The rest is a calculation of delay.
